text: The firmware emulates a minimal ESPHome native API device (plaintext, TCP 6053) so the user's existing havpe-server (Go, Silero VAD on the server, ElevenLabs STT/TTS, webhook + regex shortcuts) can drive it unchanged. Rejected: a new WebSocket protocol in havpe-server (duplicates a working pipeline, two device protocols to maintain). The device advertises mDNS hostname prefix home-assistant-voice- because havpe-server discovers by that prefix; this is safe only because the user's real Voice PE is no longer in use (two matching devices make the server refuse to start).

Wake word is 'Alexa' via ESP-SR WakeNet9s. The user wanted 'whatever microWakeWord has'; Alexa is the only phrase both microWakeWord and WakeNet9s ship. Running microWakeWord (TFLite Micro) on the ESP32-C6 was rejected: no SIMD/esp-nn acceleration and no FPU on the C6. Silero VAD on the device was rejected for the same reasons plus RAM (about 2 MB float model); end-of-speech detection stays on the server.

Reply audio: havpe-server serves ElevenLabs MP3 plus 44.1/48 kHz WAV tones by URL. The user prefers decoding MP3 on the device (esp_audio_codec). Agreed fallback if RAM does not allow it: change havpe-server to request pcm_16000 from ElevenLabs and serve WAV, so the device only decodes WAV. The user pre-approved this fallback.
Builds use the espressif/idf:v5.5.3 Docker image instead of a local ESP-IDF install (the user's machine only has an old IDF 4.4 environment). v5.5.3 matches Waveshare's examples.

The board lives on the user's main network (192.168.10.x, same subnet as havpe-server at 192.168.10.4), not the IoT VLAN. The IoT VLAN (192.168.13.x) blocks new connections from the board to the main LAN, which broke fetching reply audio from havpe-server's HTTP port 8085; the API connection only worked because the server opens it. The user gave the board a fixed IP (192.168.10.206) and points havpe-server at it; mDNS discovery also works on this subnet.

The user decided KEY (GPIO10) mutes and unmutes the microphone instead of starting a voice session; the wake word is the only session trigger. Mute fully releases the microphone (privacy, like the Voice PE mute switch). A press during a session takes effect when the session returns to idle. Mute state is not persisted: the board always boots unmuted.

The user accepts GPL for this firmware and prefers AGPL. So GPLv3 code from ESPHome (micro_wake_word C++) may be reused for the planned microWakeWord port; the project licence should be AGPL-3.0 (GPLv3 code can be combined into an AGPLv3 work).

Face screen decisions from the user: only 8 faces (idle_default, listening, thinking, speaking, muted, blink, idle_happy_eyes, idle_curious) out of a 21-face set; the rest stay out of the repo. Plain black background (AMOLED power and burn-in). Burn-in protection: the user pointed out that a few-pixel drift leaves eye centres always lit, so the agreed measures are idle dimming (about 25% after 30 s idle, full during sessions) plus a slow ±20 px drift, blink and short variety faces. Rejected: alpha-only (A8) tinted images (lose the pink accents), compressed LVGL images (need full RAM decode), a separate flash partition (not needed once the set is small).
